page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6149 processor running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, with 2 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. The processor includes a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 22 MB L3 cache. It supports instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.hfg5.large resides in the lower performance tiers across multiple categories. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance is rated as weak, while the multi-core CPU performance falls into the poor category. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block speed of 100.02 GB/sec, but large block read and write speeds drop to 9.96 GB/sec and 9.61 GB/sec respectively, both placing in the bottom 10% of tested instances. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1076.0 and a multi-core score of 1279.0. Similarly, Passmark CPU and memory scores are positioned in the bottom 10%, with database operations scoring 609.36 and encryption scoring 827.11.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.hfg5.large offers dedicated CPU resources but exhibits limited computational and memory throughput relative to modern high-density instances. The absence of local storage and GPUs, combined with its low benchmark scores, suggests a tradeoff where dedicated CPU allocation is prioritized over high-speed data processing. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is suitable for entry-level workloads that require dedicated CPU cores without demanding high memory bandwidth or intensive parallel processing. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, basic text processing, simple database operations, and low-throughput background tasks.
